mainTopic: Doubtful כיסוי הדם on יום טוב, and whether a slaughter that does not permit the meat counts as a slaughter for אותו ואת בנו and כיסוי הדם.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about the blood of a כוי, an animal whose status is a doubt. The question is whether a doubtful כיסוי הדם may be done on יום טוב. A comparison to a טומטום blowing שופר fails twice. רבי יוסי lets even a woman blow, as he lets women do סמיכה. For the רבנן, שופר is stronger because it overrides שבת in the מקדש. רבי אלעזר הקפר also breaks the קל וחומר from מילה, since מילה is only done by day, and רבי אבא praises this answer. A new משנה then argues whether a slaughter that does not make the meat permitted still requires כיסוי הדם: רבי מאיר says yes and חכמים say no. The גמרא reports that רבי ruled like רבי מאיר for אותו ואת בנו and like רבי שמעון for כיסוי הדם, and traces each side's sources from the פסוקים. The amud ends as רבי אבא begins a new statement, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The doubt in the שופר case is about whether the person is a man or a woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ספק in the שופר case is a person whose gender is uncertain (a טומטום), who still blows on ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the doubt is whether the person is a man or a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering the question "what kind of doubt does שופר involve?" It answers that the doubt is about a person who might be a man or might be a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Men must blow שופר and women are not obligated. A טומטום might be either, so his obligation is only a ספק, yet he still blows on יום טוב. This looks like a model for doing a doubtful מצוה, like covering the blood of a כוי, on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejects the earlier option and gives a new one)
A doubt or uncertainty
A person who may be a man or may be a woman (such as a טומטום)

phrases.english: Rather, a doubt whether a man
phrases.notes: This means someone like a טומטום, whose body doesn't make clear whether he is a man or a woman.

phrases.english: or a woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא סְפֵק אִישׁ סְפֵק אִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the earlier question about what kind of doubt the שופר case involves.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of ספק in שופר could serve as a model for the כוי?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A person of doubtful gender, who blows שופר even though his obligation is uncertain.

steps.title: רבי יוסי holds that even a woman may blow the שופר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי יוסי is consistent with his own view, because he holds that even a definite woman may blow שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי follows his own reasoning, since he says that even a definite woman may blow the שופר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבי יוסי holds that even a woman who is certainly a woman may blow שופר on ראש השנה. It is setting up a source for this in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even a woman, who is not obligated, may blow, then a טומטום blowing proves nothing special about a doubtful מצוה overriding יום טוב. Blowing is simply permitted as an optional act. So according to רבי יוסי, the שופר case is not a real model for the כוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning, consistent with his view elsewhere
Definite or certain (here: certainly a woman)
Also, even
She blows the שופר

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei follows his own reasoning,
as he says: a definite woman may also blow.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי לְטַעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that according to רבי יוסי, the טומטום case from step 1 is not a true example of a doubtful מצוה overriding יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, even a definite woman may blow שופר on ראש השנה.

steps.title: Source: women may optionally do סמיכה on a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון allow women to do סמיכה as an optional act, which is the basis for רבי יוסי's view on שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: Jewish men do סמיכה, but Jewish women do not. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say: women may do סמיכה if they choose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי יוסי lets women do מצוות they are not obligated in. The ברייתא's case is סמיכה, leaning on a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion learns from the פסוק "בני ישראל" that only men do סמיכה. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say women may do it as רשות, and leaning on the animal is not treated as forbidden use of a קרבן. In the same way, רבי יוסי lets a woman blow שופר, and we do not view it as breaking יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Do סמיכה: lean the hands on the head of a קרבן before it is slaughtered
Jewish women
Optional: allowed but not required

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source that רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון allow women to do מצוות they are not obligated in.

phrases.english: As it is taught: the sons of Israel lean their hands,
but the daughters of Israel do not lean.
Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon say:
Women may lean, as an optional act.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל סוֹמְכִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for רבי יוסי's view stated in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי's view that even a woman may blow שופר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון allow women to do סמיכה as רשות.

steps.title: רבינא: even according to the רבנן, שופר cannot be compared to כיסוי הדם
steps.stepSummary: רבינא shows that even according to the רבנן the comparison fails. When שופר is certain it overrides שבת in the מקדש, but כיסוי הדם never overrides שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: even according to what the רבנן say, there is a refutation. What is special about blowing the שופר is that when it is certain, it overrides שבת in the מקדש. Can you say the same about covering the blood, which never overrides שבת at all?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא knocks down the proof from שופר, even according to the רבנן who hold that women may not blow. He points out a way in which שופר is stronger than covering the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A certain obligation of שופר is strong enough to push aside שבת in the מקדש. So it makes sense that even its doubtful form can push aside יום טוב. כיסוי הדם never overrides שבת in any case, so a doubtful כיסוי cannot be expected to override יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation that shows a comparison does not work
"What about X, which has this special feature": the standard form for breaking a comparison
Its certain form (the definite obligation)
Overrides שבת
Covering, meaning כיסוי הדם, covering the blood after slaughtering a bird or wild animal

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from שופר fails for everyone. For רבי יוסי, women may blow anyway. For the רבנן, שופר is stronger because it overrides שבת in the מקדש, and כיסוי הדם never does.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
And even according to what the Sages say,
there is a refutation:
What about blowing the shofar,
since its definite form overrides Shabbat in the Temple,
can you say the same of covering the blood,
which does not override it at all!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאי דְּקָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן נָמֵי אִית לֵיהּ פִּירְכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing that רבי יוסי rejects the proof, רבינא shows that the רבנן cannot use it either.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole comparison of a doubtful כיסוי הדם on יום טוב to a doubtful תקיעת שופר, even according to the רבנן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שופר is stronger: its certain form overrides שבת in the מקדש, while כיסוי הדם never overrides שבת.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר הקפר breaks the comparison to מילה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר הקפר rejects learning כיסוי הדם from מילה, because מילה does not apply on the nights of יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר הקפר answered: You cannot learn from מילה. מילה is special because it does not apply on the nights of יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר הקפר pushes back against the קל וחומר that learned from מילה that a doubtful כיסוי הדם does not push aside יום טוב. He points out a way that מילה is weaker.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the source case is at least as strong as the new case. רבי אלעזר הקפר says מילה has a limitation that כיסוי הדם does not have, so a rule about מילה cannot be carried over to כיסוי הדם.

keyTerms.meaning: Circumcision
"What about...?": the standard opening for showing that a source case is special and cannot be compared
The nights of the Festivals
Applies, is in effect

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar HaKappar the Distinguished responded:
What about circumcision?
It is special in that it does not apply
on the nights of Festivals.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵשִׁיב רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הַקַּפָּר בְּרִיבִּי מָה לְמִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא about the כוי (from the previous amud) with a further refutation of רבי יוסי's קל וחומר from מילה
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר that learns doubtful כיסוי הדם from doubtful מילה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: מילה has a time limitation (it does not apply at night) that כיסוי הדם lacks, so מילה is the weaker case

steps.title: Does מילה apply on ordinary nights?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording: saying 'Festival nights' implies that מילה applies on other nights, which is false.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it only on the nights of יום טוב that מילה does not apply, while on other nights it does?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions how רבי אלעזר הקפר phrased his point. If he says מילה does not apply on Festival nights, that sounds as if it does apply on regular nights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מילה is never done at night at all, so mentioning Festival nights specifically seems wrong. The challenge is aimed at the wording of the rebuttal, not at its basic idea.

keyTerms.meaning: Applies (Aramaic form)
Other nights, ordinary nights

phrases.aramaic: בְּלֵילֵי יָמִים טוֹבִים הוּא דְּלָא נָהֲגָא,
phrases.english: Is it only on Festival nights that it does not apply,
but on other nights it does apply?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּלֵילֵי יָמִים טוֹבִים הוּא דְּלָא נָהֲגָא בִּשְׁאָר לֵילֵי נָהֲגָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the rebuttal in step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'אינה נוהגת בלילי ימים טובים'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Singling out Festival nights implies that מילה applies on other nights, but מילה never applies at night

steps.title: Corrected wording: מילה never applies at night
steps.stepSummary: The rebuttal is restated: מילה does not apply at night at all, but כיסוי הדם applies both day and night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say this: מילה is special because it does not apply at night as it does by day. Can you say the same about כיסוי הדם, which applies at night just as by day?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of רבי אלעזר הקפר's point. The real difference is that מילה is limited to daytime, while כיסוי הדם has no time limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the rebuttal is accurate. Because מילה is restricted to daytime, it is a weaker מצוה, and its rules cannot be carried over to כיסוי הדם, which applies around the clock.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: introduces a corrected version
At night as by day
Will you say? (that the same rule applies)
Covering (the blood)

steps.whatToRemember: The difference is that מילה is a daytime-only מצוה, while כיסוי הדם applies both day and night, so the קל וחומר from מילה fails.

phrases.english: Rather: what about circumcision?
It is special in that it does not apply at night as it does by day.
Will you say the same about covering,
which applies at night just as by day!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מָה לְמִילָה שֶׁכֵּן אֵינָהּ נוֹהֶגֶת בַּלֵּילוֹת כְּבַיָּמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 by correcting the wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rebuttal seemed to be about Festival nights specifically
steps.terutzMaskana: The rebuttal is about nighttime in general: מילה is limited to the day, while כיסוי applies day and night

steps.title: רבי אבא praises the refutation
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא says this was one of the arguments רבי חייא called unanswerable, yet רבי אלעזר found an answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: This is one of the arguments that רבי חייא said had no answer, and רבי אלעזר the Distinguished gave an answer.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא closes the discussion by noting how impressive this rebuttal is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא had considered the קל וחומר from מילה airtight. רבי אבא tells us that רבי אלעזר הקפר's point about nighttime successfully broke it, so the rebuttal stands.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no refutation for them
He gave a refutation

steps.whatToRemember: The קל וחומר from מילה, which רבי חייא thought was unanswerable, is broken by רבי אלעזר הקפר's point that מילה is daytime-only.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: זֶה אֶחָד מִן הַדְּבָרִים
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said: This is one of the matters

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא אֵין עֲלֵיהֶן תְּשׁוּבָה,
phrases.english: about which Rabbi Chiyya said there is no refutation for them,
phrases.notes: "This" is the קל וחומר from circumcision.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Elazar the Distinguished gave a refutation.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה אֶחָד מִן הַדְּבָרִים שֶׁאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא אֵין עֲלֵיהֶן תְּשׁוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Wraps up the rebuttal with praise from רבי אבא
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אלעזר הקפר's rebuttal succeeds, even though רבי חייא had considered the קל וחומר unanswerable

steps.title: New משנה: slaughters unfit for eating
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists slaughters whose meat may not be eaten. רבי מאיר requires כיסוי הדם for them and חכמים exempt them.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who slaughters and the animal turns out to be a טריפה; one who slaughters for עבודה זרה; one who slaughters a non-sacred animal inside the עזרה or a sacrificial one outside; and an undomesticated animal or bird that was sentenced to stoning: רבי מאיר obligates covering the blood, and חכמים exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists cases where the slaughter itself was done, but the meat is forbidden to eat, and asks whether the blood must be covered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that the slaughtering act alone creates the obligation of כיסוי הדם. חכמים hold that a slaughter which does not make the meat permitted does not count as a real slaughter for this מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat
Idol worship
Non-sacred animals slaughtered inside the Temple courtyard, and sacrificial animals slaughtered outside it
Sentenced to stoning
Obligates / exempt

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One who slaughters, and it is found to be a treifah,
and one who slaughters for idol worship,
and one who slaughters non-sacred animals inside
phrases.notes: "Inside" means inside the Temple courtyard, and "outside" means outside it.

phrases.english: or sacrificial animals outside,
an undomesticated animal or bird sentenced to stoning:
Rabbi Meir obligates,
and the Sages exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַשּׁוֹחֵט וְנִמְצֵאת טְרֵיפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה on a new topic within the laws of כיסוי הדם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In slaughters that do not make the meat permitted, רבי מאיר requires כיסוי הדם and חכמים exempt

steps.title: No covering when there was no valid slaughter
steps.stepSummary: If the slaughter was invalid (נבילה), or the animal was stabbed or torn, there is no obligation of כיסוי הדם.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who slaughters and it becomes a carcass in his hand, one who stabs, and one who tears: he is exempt from covering.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with cases where no proper slaughter happened at all. Here everyone agrees there is no need to cover the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier cases a technically valid slaughter took place, which is why רבי מאיר required covering. Here there was no valid שחיטה at all, so even רבי מאיר agrees there is no obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: Became a נבילה (carcass) in his hand through a faulty slaughter
One who stabs the animal instead of slaughtering it
One who tears out the windpipe and gullet
Exempt from covering the blood

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the earlier list. There, the slaughter itself was valid and only the meat was forbidden, so רבי מאיר requires covering. Here the slaughter itself failed, so there is no dispute.

phrases.english: One who slaughters and it became a carcass in his hand,
phrases.notes: The slaughter was done incorrectly, so the animal never became kosher.

phrases.english: one who stabs and one who tears loose,
is exempt from covering.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשּׁוֹחֵט וְנִתְנַבְּלָה בְּיָדוֹ הַנּוֹחֵר וְהַמְעַקֵּר פָּטוּר מִלְּכַסּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with cases of invalid slaughter, which everyone exempts
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An invalid slaughter, stabbing, or tearing creates no obligation of כיסוי הדם

steps.title: רבי sided with different תנאים in each משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reports that רבי followed רבי מאיר for אותו ואת בנו and רבי שמעון for כיסוי הדם. In both places he recorded the view he agreed with as the view of 'חכמים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: רבי agreed with רבי מאיר about the law of אותו ואת בנו and wrote it as the view of חכמים. He also agreed with רבי שמעון about כיסוי הדם and wrote that as the view of חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by telling us how רבי, who arranged the משנה, decided between רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון. He sided with a different one in each of the two topics.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether an unfit slaughter (שחיטה שאינה ראויה) counts as a slaughter. For אותו ואת בנו, רבי agreed it counts, like רבי מאיר. For כיסוי הדם, he agreed it does not count, like רבי שמעון. In both places he wrote the view he accepted under the name 'חכמים' so that people would follow it.

keyTerms.meaning: The ban on slaughtering a mother animal and its young on the same day
Under the label 'the Sages', meaning written as the anonymous majority view
He taught it, meaning he recorded it in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: In our משנה, the 'חכמים' who exempt unfit slaughters from כיסוי הדם are really רבי שמעון. רבי just wrote his view as 'חכמים'. So in this משנה, 'חכמים' does not mean a separate group of sages.
steps.whyThisMatters: This tells us the practical halacha: an unfit slaughter counts for אותו ואת בנו but not for כיסוי הדם.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: רָאָה רַבִּי דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי מֵאִיר
phrases.english: Rabbi saw the words of Rabbi Meir as correct
phrases.notes: 'רבי' alone means רבי יהודה הנשיא, who arranged the משנה.

phrases.english: regarding 'it and its offspring,'
and he taught it in the name of the Sages,
and those of Rabbi Shimon regarding covering the blood,
and he taught it in the name of the Sages.
phrases.notes: That is our משנה, where the 'חכמים' exempt unfit slaughters from covering the blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָאָה רַבִּי דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה from steps 9-10 and explains who the anonymous 'חכמים' are.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For אותו ואת בנו the halacha follows רבי מאיר: an unfit slaughter counts. For כיסוי הדם the halacha follows רבי שמעון: an unfit slaughter does not count.

steps.title: What is רבי מאיר's source for אותו ואת בנו?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי מאיר holds that an unfit slaughter counts as a slaughter for אותו ואת בנו.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי מאיר's reason regarding אותו ואת בנו?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source behind רבי מאיר's view. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that is not made kosher by its slaughter might not seem to be 'slaughtered' at all. The גמרא wants to know why רבי מאיר still treats it as a slaughter for this prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Meir
regarding 'it and its offspring'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the view רבי accepted in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for treating an unfit slaughter as a slaughter for אותו ואת בנו.

steps.title: רבי מאיר learns from slaughtering sacrifices outside
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says רבי מאיר links the word 'slaughter' in אותו ואת בנו to the same word in שחוטי חוץ. An outside slaughter is unfit, yet it still counts as a slaughter. So here too an unfit slaughter counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: He learns 'slaughter, slaughter' from sacrifices slaughtered outside the Temple. Just as there an unfit slaughter is still called a slaughter, so here too an unfit slaughter is called a slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי מאיר uses a word-link (a גזרה שוה) between two verses that both use the word 'slaughter'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who slaughters a קרבן outside the Temple is liable, even though that meat is forbidden and the slaughter makes nothing permitted. So in that law, an unfit slaughter still counts as a slaughter. The shared word carries this idea over to אותו ואת בנו.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it, here through a word-link between verses
Sacrificial animals slaughtered outside the Temple, which is forbidden
A slaughter that does not make the meat permitted
It is still called a slaughter

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
He derives 'slaughter' and 'slaughter'
phrases.notes: The two verses are ויקרא 22:28 (אותו ואת בנו) and ויקרא 17:3 (slaughtering outside).

phrases.english: from animals slaughtered outside the Temple.
Just as there,
a slaughter that is not fit
is called a slaughter,
so too here,
a slaughter that is not fit
is called a slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּמַר שְׁחִיטָה שְׁחִיטָה מִשְּׁחוּטֵי חוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A word-link with שחוטי חוץ, where an unfit slaughter still makes the person liable, shows that an unfit slaughter counts for אותו ואת בנו too.

steps.title: What is רבי שמעון's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון holds that an unfit slaughter is not a slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון, what is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for the source on the other side. This sets up רבי שמעון's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי מאיר has a strong word-link from שחוטי חוץ, the גמרא needs to show what text רבי שמעון relies on to reach the opposite conclusion.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon, what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי מאיר's source to the opposing view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for רבי שמעון's view that an unfit slaughter is not a slaughter.

steps.title: רבי שמעון learns from יוסף's meal
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני בר פטיש says רבי שמעון learns from 'טבוח טבח והכן', a slaughter for eating. That was a fit slaughter, so only a fit slaughter counts here too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מני בר פטיש said: He learns from 'Slaughter the animal and prepare.' Just as there it was a fit slaughter, so here too it means a fit slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון learns from a different verse, where slaughter clearly means slaughtering an animal to eat it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק about יוסף's meal, the slaughter was done so the meat could be eaten, so it was a fit slaughter. רבי שמעון takes this as the basic meaning of 'slaughter'. So a slaughter that does not permit the meat is not called a slaughter.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Slaughter an animal and prepare': יוסף's order for the meal with his brothers
A fit slaughter, one that makes the meat permitted

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר learns from שחוטי חוץ that an unfit slaughter counts. רבי שמעון learns from 'טבוח טבח והכן' that only a fit slaughter counts. Halacha: like רבי מאיר for אותו ואת בנו, and like רבי שמעון for כיסוי הדם.

phrases.english: Rabbi Mani bar Pattish said:
He derives it from 'Slaughter the animal and prepare,'
just as there it is a fit slaughter,
so too here it means a fit slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּמַר מִטְּבוֹחַ טֶבַח וְהָכֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Learning from 'טבוח טבח והכן', where the slaughter was fit for eating, shows that 'slaughter' means only a fit slaughter.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי מאיר also learn from 'טבוח'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי מאיר does not use רבי שמעון's source, 'טבוח טבח', which would teach that only a fit slaughter counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר too, why not learn from 'טבוח'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי מאיר: there is a perfectly good source, the one רבי שמעון uses, so why does רבי מאיר ignore it? This sets up the next step, where the גמרא answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15, רבי שמעון learned from 'טבוח טבח' that only a fit slaughter counts. If רבי מאיר accepted that source too, he would reach the opposite result from his own view. So the גמרא wants to know why רבי מאיר does not use it.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him learn it from, meaning derive it from
Slaughter, a different word for slaughtering, from the פסוק 'טבוח טבח והכן'

phrases.english: And רבי מאיר as well,
let him learn it from 'טבוח'!
phrases.notes: This is the source רבי שמעון used in step 15: 'טבוח טבח והכן', a slaughter meant for eating.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר נָמֵי, לִיגְמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי מאיר using רבי שמעון's source from step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's choice of שחוטי חוץ as his source
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is another source, 'טבוח', that would teach only a fit slaughter counts. Why does רבי מאיר not use it?

steps.title: Learn שחיטה only from the same word שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that you compare the word שחיטה to another שחיטה, not to the different word טביחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn 'שחיטה' from 'שחיטה', and we do not learn 'שחיטה' from 'טביחה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי מאיר: אותו ואת בנו uses the word שחיטה. So he learns from another place that uses the same word, which is שחוטי חוץ, and not from a place that uses a different word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק of אותו ואת בנו says 'לא תשחטו', and שחוטי חוץ also uses a form of שחיטה. 'טבוח' is a different word, even though it means the same thing. רבי מאיר holds that an exact word match is the better source.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn, meaning we derive one law from another
Slaughter, the word used in אותו ואת בנו and in שחוטי חוץ
Slaughter, using a different Hebrew word

phrases.english: We learn 'שחיטה' from 'שחיטה',
and we do not learn 'שחיטה' from 'טביחה'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rule about which source is better: the same word beats a word with the same meaning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any word meaning 'slaughter' could serve as a source
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the exact same word, שחיטה, is used as the source

steps.title: Different words with the same meaning can still be compared
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: דבי רבי ישמעאל compared 'ושב' with 'ובא', two different words with the same meaning. So why can't שחיטה be compared with טביחה?
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make? Didn't the school of רבי ישמעאל teach: 'And the כהן shall return' and 'And the כהן shall come'? This returning is the same as this coming.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 17. It brings a teaching showing that two different words with the same meaning can be linked to each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With צרעת of houses, דבי רבי ישמעאל compared 'ושב הכהן' with 'ובא הכהן' even though the words are different, because the meaning is the same. If so, שחיטה and טביחה, which also mean the same thing, should be comparable too. That would knock down רבי מאיר's reason.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference does it make?
Returning, from the word 'ושב'
Coming, from the word 'ובא'

phrases.english: What difference does it make?
Didn't the school of רבי ישמעאל teach:
'And the כהן shall return' and 'And the כהן shall come':
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:39 and 14:44, both about a כהן checking צרעת on a house.

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ הִיא שִׁיבָה זוֹ הִיא בִּיאָה.
phrases.english: this is returning, this is coming.
phrases.notes: He means the two words count as the same, so one can be learned from the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ? הָא תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that שחיטה cannot be learned from טביחה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: דבי רבי ישמעאל links different words with the same meaning, so the exact word should not matter

steps.title: Use a word with the same meaning only when no identical word exists
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל's method applies only when there is no identical word. When an identical word exists, we learn from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: That applies only where there is nothing identical to it. But where there is something identical to it, we learn from the identical one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי מאיר. Comparing words with the same meaning is a fallback, used only when no exact match exists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'ושב' and 'ובא' there was no exact match, so the same meaning was good enough. Here there is an exact match, שחיטה in שחוטי חוץ. So רבי מאיר prefers it over טביחה.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply only... (limits the scope of a rule)
Something identical to it
We learn it, meaning we derive it

steps.whatToRemember: An exact word match is the first choice. A different word with the same meaning is used only when no exact match exists.

phrases.english: These words apply
where there is nothing identical to it,
but where there is something identical to it,
we learn from what is identical to it.
phrases.notes: Here that is שחוטי חוץ, which uses the same word שחיטה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18 by limiting דבי רבי ישמעאל's teaching
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the cited teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Same-meaning words are always as good as identical words
steps.terutzMaskana: Same-meaning words are used only when no identical word exists

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי שמעון also learn from שחוטי חוץ?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to רבי שמעון and asks why he does not use רבי מאיר's source, שחוטי חוץ, which has the exact word match.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון too, why not learn from שחוטי חוץ?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא challenges the other side. Since an exact word match is the best source, why does רבי שמעון not learn from שחוטי חוץ? The next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 just showed that an identical word is the preferred source. שחוטי חוץ has the identical word שחיטה. If רבי שמעון used it, he would have to agree that an unfit slaughter counts, against his own view.

keyTerms.meaning: קדשים slaughtered outside the בית המקדש, which is forbidden

phrases.english: And רבי שמעון as well,
let him learn it from שחוטי חוץ!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן נָמֵי לִיגְמַר מִשְּׁחוּטֵי חוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 16, now challenging רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's choice of 'טבוח טבח' as his source
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שחוטי חוץ shares the exact word שחיטה, which step 19 says is the preferred source

steps.title: Learn חולין only from חולין
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds that a law about חולין should be learned from חולין, not from קדשים. So he does not use שחוטי חוץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn חולין from חולין, and we do not learn חולין from קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי שמעון. For him, being the same kind of animal, חולין, matters more than having the same word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אותו ואת בנו is mainly about ordinary animals, חולין. 'טבוח טבח' is about slaughtering for a meal, which is also חולין, while שחוטי חוץ is about קדשים. So each תנא follows a different preference: רבי מאיר chooses the same word, and רבי שמעון chooses the same kind of animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary animals, not holy
Holy animals set aside as קרבנות

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר compares by the same word (שחיטה from שחיטה). רבי שמעון compares by the same kind of animal (חולין from חולין). That is why they reach opposite results about an unfit slaughter.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי שמעון rejects the idea of learning from an identical word. He simply holds that matching חולין with חולין is the stronger match here.

phrases.english: We learn חולין from חולין,
and we do not learn חולין from קדשים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rule about which source is better: same kind of animal beats same word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An identical word is always the best source
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי שמעון, matching חולין with חולין comes first

steps.title: רבי מאיר: אותו ואת בנו also applies to sacrifices
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר rejects רבי שמעון's reasoning by pointing out that אותו ואת בנו also applies to קדשים, so learning from שחוטי חוץ is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר would answer: Are you saying the law of a mother and its offspring does not apply to sacrificial animals?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר answers רבי שמעון's argument from the last step: you can learn this law from קדשים, because the law itself applies to קדשים too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון said a law about חולין must be learned from חולין. רבי מאיר replies that אותו ואת בנו is not only a חולין law, since it applies to sacrificial animals too. So learning it from שחוטי חוץ, which is about sacrifices, is a fair comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (a question that shows the other idea cannot be right)
The ban on slaughtering a mother animal and its offspring on the same day
Animals set aside as sacrifices
Applies, is in force

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir [would answer]:
Is that to say that [the law of] a mother and its offspring
does not apply to sacrificial animals?
phrases.notes: The answer is obvious: it does apply. So the case is not purely a חולין case.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר: אַטּוּ אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ בְּקָדָשִׁים מִי לָא נָהֵיג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי שמעון's reason for not learning from שחוטי חוץ
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי שמעון's rule that חולין must be learned only from חולין, as applied to אותו ואת בנו
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אותו ואת בנו also applies to קדשים, so learning it from קדשים is not comparing two unrelated areas

steps.title: רבי accepted רבי מאיר's view on אותו ואת בנו
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא reports that רבי agreed with רבי מאיר about אותו ואת בנו and placed his view in the משנה as the opinion of 'the Sages'.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי חייא meant when he said: רבי saw that רבי מאיר's words about אותו ואת בנו were correct, and he taught them in the name of חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the אותו ואת בנו discussion by showing that רבי sided with רבי מאיר there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When רבי, who arranged the משנה, writes a view without a name, as 'the Sages' or with no name at all, he is presenting it as the accepted view. So in the משנה about אותו ואת בנו, the unnamed view is really רבי מאיר's, and רבי chose it.

keyTerms.meaning: Saw. Here it means he agreed with it or saw it as correct
And he taught it (in the משנה)
In the name of 'the Sages', as the unnamed, accepted view

steps.whatToRemember: In the אותו ואת בנו case, רבי sided with רבי מאיר: a slaughter that does not permit the meat still counts as a slaughter.

phrases.english: This is what Rabbi Chiyya meant when he said:

phrases.aramaic: רָאָה רַבִּי דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי מֵאִיר
phrases.english: Rabbi saw [as correct] the words of Rabbi Meir
phrases.notes: 'רבי' alone means רבי יהודה הנשיא, the one who put the משנה together.

phrases.english: regarding a mother and its offspring,
and taught it in the name of 'the Sages.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ דְּקָאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties רבי מאיר's successful defense to how רבי wrote the משנה
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For אותו ואת בנו, רבי accepted רבי מאיר's view and taught it as the view of the Sages.

steps.title: What is רבי מאיר's source for covering the blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new topic and asks why רבי מאיר requires כיסוי הדם after a slaughter that does not permit the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי מאיר's reason regarding covering the blood?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new discussion. It moves from אותו ואת בנו to the מצוה of כיסוי הדם and asks for רבי מאיר's source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the כיסוי הדם case, רבי מאיר says you must cover the blood even when the slaughter did not make the meat permitted. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק or derivation he relies on for this.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? (asks for the source or logic)
The מצוה to cover the blood after slaughtering a wild animal or bird

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Meir
regarding covering the blood?
phrases.notes: He means a slaughter that turned out not to permit the meat, the same kind of case as before.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּכִסּוּי הַדָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from אותו ואת בנו to the parallel argument about כיסוי הדם
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי מאיר's view that a slaughter which does not permit the meat still requires covering the blood

steps.title: ריש לקיש: רבי מאיר learns 'pouring' from sacrifices slaughtered outside
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that רבי מאיר learns a גזירה שוה from the word 'pouring' in שחוטי חוץ. There, a slaughter that does not permit the meat still counts as a slaughter, and the same is true for כיסוי הדם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: He learns 'pouring' from 'pouring' in the case of sacrifices slaughtered outside the Temple. Just as there, a slaughter that is not fit is still called a slaughter, so too here, a slaughter that is not fit is still called a slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives רבי מאיר's source: the same word, 'pouring', appears in both places, so the two laws are linked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who slaughters a sacrifice outside the עזרה is liable even though that slaughter cannot make the meat permitted. Because both פסוקים use the word 'pouring', רבי מאיר applies the same idea to כיסוי הדם. This matches what we saw in Step 17: רבי מאיר prefers learning from an identical word.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns (one law from another)
Pouring (out blood)
Sacrifices slaughtered outside the Temple courtyard
A slaughter that does not make the meat permitted
Just as there... so too here (the comparison formula)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
He learns 'pouring' from 'pouring'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:13 (covering the blood) and ויקרא 17:4 (slaughtering outside).

phrases.english: from [sacrifices] slaughtered outside [the Temple].
Just as there,
a slaughter that is not fit
is called a slaughter,
so too here,
a slaughter that is not fit
is called a slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: גָּמַר שְׁפִיכָה שְׁפִיכָה מִשְּׁחוּטֵי חוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 24
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of 'pouring' and 'pouring' from שחוטי חוץ teaches that an unfit slaughter still counts as a slaughter for כיסוי הדם.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the פסוק says 'that may be eaten'
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון points to the words אשר יאכל in the פסוק of כיסוי הדם. They suggest the מצוה applies only when the slaughter makes the animal fit to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון would say: It is written, 'that may be eaten.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון challenges רבי מאיר's derivation with words from the כיסוי הדם פסוק itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of a wild animal or bird 'that may be eaten'. To רבי שמעון this means you only cover the blood when the slaughter produced edible meat. So a slaughter that does not permit the meat needs no covering, whatever the גזירה שוה says.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That may be eaten', words in the פסוק of covering the blood
It is written

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon [would say]:
'that may be eaten' is written,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: ״אֲשֶׁר יֵאָכֵל״ כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי שמעון's source against רבי מאיר's derivation
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's view that an unfit slaughter requires covering the blood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק limits covering to an animal 'that may be eaten', and an unfit slaughter does not produce edible meat.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: 'that may be eaten' excludes a non-kosher bird
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר answers that אשר יאכל has a different job: it excludes a non-kosher bird from the מצוה of covering the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר would say: That phrase comes to exclude a non-kosher bird.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר defends himself by giving the words 'that may be eaten' a different purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the words are needed to teach something else, they cannot also teach רבי שמעון's point. רבי מאיר says they teach that a species that is not kosher, like a non-kosher bird, needs no covering. They say nothing about a kosher animal whose slaughter failed.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude
A non-kosher bird
That is what it comes [to teach]

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir [would say]:
that [phrase is] to exclude a non-kosher bird
that it comes [to teach],

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר: הָהוּא לְמַעוֹטֵי עוֹף טָמֵא הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי שמעון's challenge by reassigning the phrase
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirecting the פסוק to a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'That may be eaten' seems to exclude any slaughter that does not produce edible meat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase only excludes non-kosher species, like a non-kosher bird.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: a טרפה is just like a non-kosher bird
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון answers that a non-kosher bird is excluded only because it cannot be eaten, and a טרפה cannot be eaten either, so it should also be excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון would say: Why is a non-kosher bird excluded? Because it is not fit to eat. A טרפה is also not fit to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון rejects רבי מאיר's answer by showing that the reason for excluding a non-kosher bird also covers a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר wanted to limit the phrase to non-kosher species. רבי שמעון says that what matters is the reason behind the rule, which is 'it cannot be eaten'. That reason applies just as well to an animal that turned out to be a טרפה, so the phrase excludes both.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit to be eaten
An animal with a fatal defect, which may not be eaten even after a proper slaughter
Also

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon [would say]:
A non-kosher bird, what is the reason [it is excluded]?
Because it is not fit to be eaten.
A טרפה also
is not fit to be eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: עוֹף טָמֵא מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי מאיר's narrow reading of 'that may be eaten'
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי מאיר's claim that the phrase excludes only a non-kosher bird
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The reason for excluding a non-kosher bird, that it is not edible, applies equally to a טרפה

steps.title: רבי accepted רבי שמעון's view on covering the blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא reports that for כיסוי הדם, רבי agreed with רבי שמעון and placed his view in the משנה as the view of 'the Sages'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what רבי חייא meant when he said: רבי saw that רבי שמעון's words about כיסוי הדם were correct, and he taught them in the name of חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the כיסוי הדם discussion by showing that here, unlike with אותו ואת בנו, רבי sided with רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי did not pick one side for both cases. In אותו ואת בנו he accepted רבי מאיר, because that law also applies to קדשים. In כיסוי הדם he accepted רבי שמעון, because of the words אשר יאכל.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי split the ruling. For אותו ואת בנו, an unfit slaughter still counts (רבי מאיר). For כיסוי הדם, an unfit slaughter does not require covering the blood (רבי שמעון).
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume 'the Sages' in the משנה always means the same תנא. Here, in one case it is רבי מאיר's view and in the other it is רבי שמעון's.

phrases.english: And this is what Rabbi Chiyya meant when he said:

phrases.aramaic: רָאָה רַבִּי דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: Rabbi saw [as correct] the words of Rabbi Shimon
regarding covering the blood,
and taught it in the name of 'the Sages.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא: רָאָה רַבִּי דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּכִסּוּי הַדָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the כיסוי הדם debate in רבי שמעון's favor and mirrors Step 23
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For כיסוי הדם, רבי accepted רבי שמעון's view that an unfit slaughter does not require covering, and taught it as the view of the Sages.

steps.title: רבי אבא begins a new statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a new statement by the אמורא רבי אבא, continuing the discussion about כיסוי הדם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא says:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. The גמרא is opening a new statement by רבי אבא, and what he actually says comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we heard the debate between רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון, and רבי חייא's report that רבי sided with רבי שמעון for כיסוי הדם. Now a new voice, the אמורא רבי אבא, is about to add something to this discussion. Nothing new has been ruled yet; wait for the next line to see his point.

keyTerms.meaning: A statement or teaching said by an אמורא, a sage of the גמרא
A sage from the time of the גמרא, coming after the sages of the משנה
The מצוה to cover the blood after slaughtering a wild animal or bird, the topic still under discussion

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for a ruling in this line. It only tells you who is speaking. The content of רבי אבא's statement is in the text that follows.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba says:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows רבי חייא's report that רבי ruled like רבי שמעון on כיסוי הדם, and opens a further statement on the same topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This line only introduces רבי אבא as the next speaker; his statement comes in the following text.
